atAGlance: Chạo tôm is grilled shrimp paste on sugarcane, usually served with herbs, rice paper, noodles, and fish-sauce dip.
whatItIs: Chạo tôm is springy shrimp paste wrapped around sugarcane and grilled. You pull off the shrimp, wrap it with herbs and rice paper if served, then dip for a sweet, smoky, seafood-rich bite.
howToEnjoy: Slide the shrimp paste from the sugarcane, build a bite with herbs, noodles, and rice paper if provided, then dip lightly. The sugarcane gives aroma more than something to chew through.
howLocalsOrder: Order chạo tôm as a shared starter or roll-your-own plate. Ask for extra rice paper, extra herbs, or no chili in the fish-sauce dip before the plate arrives.
worthKnowing: Chạo tôm is associated with central Vietnamese celebration food, especially Huế-style spreads where grilled, wrapped, and dipped bites matter.
goodToKnow: Contains or may contain seafood or shellfish.
travelerCaution: Contains or may contain seafood or shellfish.
